summary: 40 units reviewed (u83-122). No wrong identifications found; standard ones (gosarga, kāmalā, bhagandara, candana, uśīra, kuṅkuma) and probable/disputed ones (masūrikā, kiṇa, āla, ūrdhvaśvāsa, śaivāla, lepa-jvara) are tagged. Fixes: Hindi hedge for disputed śaivāla (u93) and ūrdhvaśvāsa gloss (u107); Hindi gloss for śakti=spear (u98); unintelligible u118 translations; u84 word list now carries the adopted conjectural upataptasya; 10th-class verbs wrongly marked caus. (u90, 98, 103, 108); u113 siddha 'successful' and avacārita 'applied'; Hindi drug/gender/gloss tidy-ups (u96, 99, 109, 114, 116, 122). GROUPING: 100-101 is already a complete sentence (ends 'āturo na sa jīvati'), so 102-106 is a second sentence; draft claimed one clause 100-106. Untouched and acceptable: u88/u98 flags (visarga/anusvara slips, correct, not adopted), u104 hṛṣṭa and u101 vaktra conjectures (marked in both languages), u116 (low). Human decisions: u105 kṣveḍ 'humming' vs 'murmuring'; u91 (low, number/gender disagreement with 94); u93 kuṅkuma-āla vs kuṅkuma-ala and the cockscomb alternative; u116 emendation; u92 kuṇapa and dhvāṅkṣa as two smells.
glossary_suggestions: kṣveḍ: decide 'humming' vs 'murmuring' (Hindi गुनगुनाना suggests singing).
siddha of medicines/signs in the riṣṭa chapters = 'successful' (सफल) where the next clause has siddhyati 'succeeds'; 'cooked' stays for preparations.
Hindi śakti (weapon) = शक्ति यानी भाला; dhvaja = ध्वज यानी पताका.
Hindi ऊर्ध्वश्वास = ऊर्ध्वश्वास यानी सम्भवतः कष्टपूर्ण श्वास (probable).
Hindi disputed śaivāla: 'शैवाल यानी काई जैसी जल की वनस्पति, जिसकी ठीक पहचान विवादित है'.
Chapter colophon Hindi: 'इस प्रकार <name> नामक N अध्याय' with the name unhyphenated; English ends with a full stop.
Verbs in -ayati of the 10th class (varjayati, tāḍayati) are not 'caus.' (applies to ch11 u90, 98, 103, 108).
